messages.author: shawnmb
messages.text:
I was listening back to @Pink_Elephants passionate defence of tanking (and re-reading the comments in favour of allowing tanking). A couple of things for Rational @krav1 to think about :

Idea #1 - Tanking is fine. We're all okay with it. We just don't want to play the games where a guy is trying to lose. The solution is therefore to allow guys to take a "gap" season, where they go 0-56, don't have to play any games, and get lottery odds according to where they finish.

*Thoughts: upon reflection this would be absurd. We could potentially have seasons where the entire lottery is made up of teams that didn't play a single game*

Idea #2 - Tanking is fine, leave things the way they are, if guys want to lose every game good for them.

Idea #3 - Tanking is no good, lets solve it by giving all teams equal lottery odds every season, no matter where you finish.

*Thoughts: this sounds fine until TBay gets first overall pick in McDavid's draft year. As long as everyone is okay with that, this would work. There could be other rules, like if you're top 5 in one season, you can't be top 5 the next (or whatever). It would be simple and clean. Based on the idea that rosters don't matter and it doesn't matter if the best players have the best pixelated players*

Idea #4 - Tanking is no good. To solve it we need more weighted lottery odds and maybe other rules that limit a team's ability to continually get high draft picks (ie. can't finish top 3 two seasons in a row, or whatever).

*Thoughts: wouldn't remove tanking but might disincentivize guys. It will allow certain GMs to work the new rules in their own favour.*

Idea #5 - Tanking is no good. To solve it, give everyone someone else's 1st round pick. This is the Nathan approach. The benefit is that it encourages people to cheer against their friends.

*Thoughts: very little downside except it would be harder for guys to manipulate the system for their own benefit.*

messages.author: GMDS
messages.text:
Idea 1, is fine, but guys who elect to do it get no more than (for example) 5% lottery odds...they'd be better off to play and win the bill

Idea 3, guys at the top are already getting another feather by snake draft and dropped guys available

Idea4 is reasonable, the  lottery odds can be adjusted, or there is a lottery, and brule teams get wheeled for their order, and limiting top x pick for x years is just another thing to track, and worry about with traded picks and will get convoluted and abuse when 1 gm knows they can't pick top5 and the other gm doesn't

Idea 5 you know my opinion

messages.author: Adolf Oliver Nipples
messages.text: Why didn’t I get a nickname like Rational Nips?

messages.author: Adolf Oliver Nipples
messages.text: I say leave it as is. I want the ability to hurl accusations.

messages.author: Ticklepuss
messages.text:
There's no rational fix for tanking so just leave it alone.  Make them struggle to play 50+ games and waste their time.  Continue to do your level best to embarrass them publicly, at least as much as possible.  

Overall, not a problem at mass.  Most teams have solid rosters outside of 2, and 1 of them doesn't care.

messages.author: Ticklepuss
messages.text: Personally. on a side note, i like the idea of setting a "boundary" that a team in the top X cannot get better than top X for X number of seasons.  Since we have this loser tournament to further screw the lowest teams, it might be good to set some sort of limits as to the very top picks over multiple seasons

messages.author: Ticklepuss

messages.author: Unholy

Something reasonable to stop the same teams being in the top 5 over-and-over again.
